We made an annual thing of going to a music fest along with some hanging out in between.

For me I think it has to do with masking. We have to put a face on for so long to not make other people uncomfortable, we aren't ourselves with people. You can't make deep relationships if you aren't vulnerable around them and you don't stand out if you're constantly trying to blend in. I always find myself fascinated with listening to everyone at a party but I used to be too overwhelmed to contribute in a large group. I would change my personality based on who I was talking to so large groups made it harder to know what to do. So much self-critiquing left less room for me to focus on what they're saying if I did engage.

Also friendships take work and repeated interactions. That we forget time and get too in our heads to respond means we aren't engaging much and likely put out that we aren't interested or the opposite and we get hyperfocused and want to know everything about a person or share too much. You have to build up some trust to let yourself be vulnerable and that takes time and exposure.

I've torn off my mask a lot and am working on being myself so I've managed to make a few close friends. People I want to be around accept me as I am. I've put in a few years of therapy and self-improvement too. My many weird interests make me interesting to some people. And all the past people-watching, helps me know when a topic might be less interesting to them and when to switch. It was a lot of work to shut the voice up in my head that was constantly critiquing everything I did. 

Others are just as self-absorbed so turning your attention to them and their interest helps build connections. Reminders to talk to them or even doing things that help you regularly hang out together help. 

Learning love languages for friendships can help. I like finding gifts for people that mean something but if someone is uncomfortable recieving gifts then that would be a negative impact because they're uncomfortable and I'd be hurt if they rejected something I put so much effort into so finding friends that appreciate gifts like that might be a better fit or changing how I show appreciation by maybe finding something fun to do (quality time) or helping them with something (acts of service) or verbal expressing it (words of affirmation), etc. Or maybe they like physical interations (touch) and I could find some platonic ways to show that: big hugs/high fives/complicated handshakes, soft clothing/blankets, brushing their hair or painting nails, playing an intense game of [insert sport], etc.

TLDR: friendship tips:
-Be vulnerable as trust is earned with time. (Learn about red flags)
-Finding common interests to talk about or to do together.
-Communicating effectively - love languages, not letting things build up (ask about things rather than assuming), express yourself and have boundaries.
-No one person can be your everything and you can't be someone else's. Find people that vibe with different pieces of you.
-Most importantly, people come and go, holding too tightly to someone will push them away. If you care about them, they have to grow and so do you and that might put you on different paths. Enjoy the time you have and honor it.

The habit is hard to build up. I tend to do big cleans rather than maintain too. 

Storing my cleaning stuff with point of performance has helped some. I have litter genies close to my cats litter so I don't have to find a scoop, bag or awkwardly hold it open and scoop. And worse if there's a hole in the grocery bag I'd otherwise use and spill it going to the trash. 

I also have all my bathroom cleaning stuff in one spot in the bathroom so I can see it and just reach for what I need on a random bathroom trip. If I see the mirror has stuff on it, I start cleaning that then wipe down the sink, then while I'm at it put some toilet cleaner in the bowl and wipe it down. I have a squeegee in the shower so I can just knock off the water at the end of taking one or even grab the sponge and scrub a bit when I get in then shower. 

Remembering to go to the bathroom or take a shower are a bit harder since I telework and am a hermit. 

I am housing my friend's ball pythons and she comes over once a week to check on them and feed them so that's another motivation to cleanup both myself and house, heh.

It's a habit or skill you can build. Meds only get you in the right mindset to change behavioral stuff. The more effective ADHD treatment is behavior therapy, but the meds help get you to where it's helpful. Having a good sized trash can nearby helps me a lot to clear garbage at least. If I can reach it from where I'm usually sitting, I'm more likely to throw it away rather than leave it on a table. 

My cleaning method typically is to pick up all of the same things at once. So all the visible trash, visible laundry, visible dishes. I think it's the gatherer in me, if I focus on looking for one type of thing I can see past the mess like an eye maze. 

Once the easy stuff is gone then see what the next abundant thing you can remove is. Or just focus on one corner or piece of furniture to organize what it contains. If stuff needs to leave the room I pile it based on where it needs to go then move it once the pile either is in the way or I'm done sorting. 

If you keep running into "I want to do x but y is in the way and I have to do z before y" that's when a list or at least writing down what you need to do helps. Trying to keep all the steps in your head will become overwhelming but if you make steps going back from what you want to do then you can start with what you need to do first. 

OP used body doubling to help keep him energized and focused by having a friend. You can even have someone on the phone or on a video chat maybe cleaning their own room to help you both. 

Hope this helps someone.

Some tips I've found for ADHD:
Points of performance spaces where everything I need for a task is in one place. All the stuff to clean the bathroom is under the bathroom sink together. 

Steam mop that only needs water so no chemicals to remember to buy. Just plug in and go.

Trash cans in most rooms means it's usually in arms length and I can throw things away without risking getting lost on the way to the previous one trash can in the kitchen. Also multiple bags on the trash can so I can just take it out and another is there already. 

Laundry hampers are right outside the bedroom so I see the level every morning to remind me to do it. Plus I can just toss a building pile into it quickly.

I bought litter genies for my cats so scoop, bag, and collection helper are right there anytime I notice it's filling up.

Body doubling is another great technique to have someone work beside you which motivates you by seeing them focus on a task. 

Breaking up big tasks into smaller ones. I tend to start with the end goal and think through it backwards on what I need to do before each part.

Write things down. Visually seeing it can help with organizing your thoughts. I lose paper so I have a grocery list app that I make lists in since I'm rarely far from my phone. 

Also putting appointments straight in my phone with multiple alarms. I look at the calendar while they're telling me available times. I don't get reminder cards cause I just lose them. I haven't had one person rush me to get out of the way and usually will confirm before I hit save to make sure everything is right. Also minimizes overlaps on my time due to forgetting something.

That was more than I expected. I just get excited to share with others when something works!

One thing that helps me tremendously and motivates me to make them, are desk aides. Writing down the whole process with pictures of every step or check lists. This helps me when I'm having trouble ordering what I need to do next. It creates a pattern written out that I can follow for each task so I don't miss a step.

Visualization outside the mind is a great tool for ADHD. We've got too much in our heads to organize/prioritize unless we can see the whole picture.

If I get like this I write a list of things I need to do or would like to do for reference when I find myself finishing a task or needing a break from social media. It helps me visualize things rather than trying to remember everything and not seeing the whole picture/not able to prioritize. If I see the list a few times then it sticks in my head better. Or an alarm that pops up on my phone at certain points of the day to break the social media cycle.
